sections.title: Evidence in brief
sections.html:
Take observations one and two, identical standard-normal encoders, and decoder mean zero. A shared decoder variance is optimally 2.5. The implementation substitutes variances one and four separately, giving a strictly smaller objective. Because both encoders have positive density everywhere, no shared function can equal one almost everywhere for one and four almost everywhere for the other.

\[ J_{\mathrm{shared}}=2+2\log(2.5)>2+\log4=J_{\mathrm{per\ example}} \]

findings.title: The prescribed noise estimate invalidates the central universal forecasting bound
findings.source_heading: ## Issue 2018__accepted__v19-17-777__I01 — The prescribed noise estimate invalidates the central universal forecasting bound
findings.markdown:
**Exact location.** PDF p.14, Section 4.2.2, Corollary 4, Eq. (26), with the universal threshold (20) on p.12 and variance estimate (12) on p.9. The unsupported concentration claim is Appendix C, p.35, event E2. The dependent proof is Appendix E.3.2, pp.45–46, especially (64)–(68). The abstract p.1 and contributions p.3 advertise the resulting noise-dependent counterfactual error guarantee.

**Claim.** Under the model on pp.5–6 and 11, observations are M_it plus independent, zero-mean noise with common variance sigma²; donor observations are independently retained with probability p. All observations and means are bounded in absolute value by one. The pre-treatment treated mean is a fixed linear combination of donor means, with no convex-weight or constant-treated-mean restriction. The forecasting setting explicitly allows fixed N while T0 grows (pp.13,35).

The universal prescription uses

    sigmahat² = sum_(t<=T0) (Y_1t - mean(Y_1))² / (T0-1),             (12)
    mu = (2+omega) sqrt[T (sigmahat² phat + phat(1-phat))],          (20)
    omega in (0.1,1).

Algorithm 1 performs SVT on the donor-only matrix, retaining singular values at least mu, and regresses the treated observations on the retained donor matrix. Corollary 4 asserts, for p >= T^(-1+zeta)/(sigma²+1), T <= alpha T0 and any eta>=0,

    MSE(Mhat_1^-) <= C1 (sigma²+1-p)/p + O(T0^(-1/2)),             (26)

with a universal positive C1. Even allowing the remainder constant to depend on fixed model quantities, the noiseless, fully observed case is asserted to have vanishing error.

**Error and evidence.** Estimate (12) measures the variation of the observations, including the deterministic time-varying signal. It is not an unbiased or consistent estimate of the noise variance in this model. This can cause threshold (20) to remove the entire signal forever.

For every even T0>=4 set T=2T0, N=2 and p=1. Let g_t=(-1)^t and use the bounded rank-one latent model

    f(theta,rho)=theta*rho,
    theta_1=1/2, theta_2=1/20, rho_t=g_t,
    M_1t=g_t/2, M_2t=g_t/20, beta*=10.

All latent values lie in a fixed compact interval. The means satisfy the required linear relation both before and after treatment. The donor pre/full ranks are both one. First take every noise variable to be zero. Degenerate zero noises are independent, have zero mean and common variance sigma²=0, and obey every stated boundedness condition. Set eta=0 and any omega in (0.1,1). The probability assumption holds, for example with zeta=1/2, and T<=alpha T0 holds with alpha=2.

The pre-treatment g values are exactly balanced, so (12) gives

    sigmahat² = T0/[4(T0-1)].

The only donor singular value is sqrt(T)/20, whereas

    mu = (2+omega) sqrt[T*T0/(4(T0-1))] > 1.05 sqrt(T).

Thus Algorithm 1 retains no singular values. Its entire estimated donor matrix is zero, and its treated prediction is zero regardless of which least-squares minimizer is selected. Consequently

    MSE(Mhat_1^-)=1/4

for every T0. Corollary 4 instead gives MSE=O(T0^(-1/2)). This is an exact asymptotic contradiction with fixed beta*=10 and fixed N=2, not a large hidden coefficient or an ambiguous finite numerical constant.

The failure also holds with strictly positive noise variance. Fix any 0<delta<=1/10 and put independent uniform +/-delta noise on both units at every time. All observations remain bounded by 3/5 for the treated unit and 3/20 for the donor. Let P denote orthogonal projection off the constant pre-treatment vector. For every noise realization,

    ||P(M_1^-+epsilon_1^-)||
      >= ||M_1^-||-||P epsilon_1^-||
      >= (1/2-delta) sqrt(T0).

Hence sigmahat² >= [T0/(T0-1)](1/2-delta)² >=4/25. The threshold exceeds (21/25)sqrt(T), while the sole observed donor singular value is at most (1/20+delta)sqrt(T) <=(3/20)sqrt(T). Again every signal is discarded and MSE=1/4 for every realization and every T0. The true variance is delta². For each fixed positive delta, taking T0 to infinity in (26) would require

    1/4 <= C1 delta².

No universal finite C1 can satisfy this for all arbitrarily small fixed positive delta. The proof's extra spectral concentration premise q>=T^(-1+zeta) also holds eventually for each such fixed positive delta, so that premise does not resolve the counterexample. Any fixed model-dependent remainder constant still multiplies a term that vanishes as T0 grows.

The exact expectation identity explains the failed proof step:

    E[sigmahat²]
      = sigma² + sum_(t<=T0)(M_1t-mean(M_1^-))²/(T0-1).

Appendix C p.35 nevertheless applies Hoeffding to assert that sigmahat² concentrates around sigma². Its event E2 is false for the time-varying model above. Equations (64)–(68) rely on that event to replace the threshold's estimated variance by the actual noise variance. The error is not cured by restoring beta-dependent constants omitted elsewhere: beta*=10 is constant throughout this counterexample, and its zero-noise right-hand side still tends to zero.

**Reason for rejection.** A central advertised contribution is a data-driven, signal-adaptive universal threshold with the first finite-sample noise-dependent forecasting bound. In an exactly rank-one bounded linear model, with complete observations and no noise, that prescription discards all useful donor information and has permanent error 1/4 instead of the claimed vanishing error. The fixed-positive-noise extension invalidates the universal sigma² scaling as well. A valid repair requires supplying the true noise variance, constructing and justifying a different noise estimator under suitable assumptions, restricting the treated signal, or replacing the guarantee. Changing a fixed threshold constant cannot handle all permitted donor/treated scale ratios. This is a change to the central prescription and its theoretical guarantee, beyond a typo or routine constant correction.

The finding does not assert that cross-validated rank choices or particular experimental curves fail. The paper explicitly uses data-driven rank/threshold selection in its experiments (pp.10,20). Nor does this counterexample refute the distinct aggregate-mean consistency result, Theorem 5, or Theorem 7's bound with its additional coefficient-estimation error term.

**Discovery method.** While tracing Corollary 4 to Appendix C, noticed that the asserted noise estimate was the sample variance of the entire time-varying treated series. Comparing the threshold with a weaker but perfectly predictive donor suggested a scale-separated rank-one counterexample.

**Verification method.** Read all 51 original PDF pages, including Appendices A–G, and continued checking the other theorems and experiments after finding this issue. Inspected full rendered pp.6,8,9,12,13,14,16,35,42,43,45,46,48,49 to verify the original model, donor-only SVT, variance prescription, constants, asymptotic regime and proof. Derived the exact noiseless and all-realization positive-noise arguments above. A paper-faithful NumPy implementation checked 288 combinations of T0, noise, seed replicate and omega; every prediction was zero with MSE exactly 1/4. Independent bounded original-PDF and analytic QA confirmed all assumptions and both contradictions. Historical author source and two primary case-study datasets were recovered and checked; bounded native and fresh simulation controls were run without attributing them to the original figures.

**Confidence: High.** The counterexample is exact, bounded, rank one, and satisfies the stated assumptions with a fixed coefficient. Its prediction is zero for algebraic reasons, and a strictly positive-noise extension avoids reliance on degeneracy. Independent original-PDF QA confirms the location, assumptions and rejection-level central consequence.

Appendix C p.35 nevertheless applies Hoeffding to assert that sigmahat² concentrates around sigma². Its event E2 is false for the time-varying model above. Equations (64)–(68) rely on that event to replace the threshold's estimated variance by the actual noise variance. The error is not cured by restoring beta-dependent constants omitted elsewhere: beta*=10 is constant throughout this counterexample, and its zero-noise right-hand side still tends to zero.

Reason for rejection.

A central advertised contribution is a data-driven, signal-adaptive universal threshold with the first finite-sample noise-dependent forecasting bound. In an exactly rank-one bounded linear model, with complete observations and no noise, that prescription discards all useful donor information and has permanent error 1/4 instead of the claimed vanishing error. The fixed-positive-noise extension invalidates the universal sigma² scaling as well. A valid repair requires supplying the true noise variance, constructing and justifying a different noise estimator under suitable assumptions, restricting the treated signal, or replacing the guarantee. Changing a fixed threshold constant cannot handle all permitted donor/treated scale ratios. This is a change to the central prescription and its theoretical guarantee, beyond a typo or routine constant correction.

The finding does not assert that cross-validated rank choices or particular experimental curves fail. The paper explicitly uses data-driven rank/threshold selection in its experiments (pp.10,20). Nor does this counterexample refute the distinct aggregate-mean consistency result, Theorem 5, or Theorem 7's bound with its additional coefficient-estimation error term.

Discovery method.

While tracing Corollary 4 to Appendix C, noticed that the asserted noise estimate was the sample variance of the entire time-varying treated series. Comparing the threshold with a weaker but perfectly predictive donor suggested a scale-separated rank-one counterexample.

Verification method.

Read all 51 original PDF pages, including Appendices A–G, and continued checking the other theorems and experiments after finding this issue. Inspected full rendered pp.6,8,9,12,13,14,16,35,42,43,45,46,48,49 to verify the original model, donor-only SVT, variance prescription, constants, asymptotic regime and proof. Derived the exact noiseless and all-realization positive-noise arguments above. A paper-faithful NumPy implementation checked 288 combinations of T0, noise, seed replicate and omega; every prediction was zero with MSE exactly 1/4. Independent bounded original-PDF and analytic QA confirmed all assumptions and both contradictions. Historical author source and two primary case-study datasets were recovered and checked; bounded native and fresh simulation controls were run without attributing them to the original figures.

Confidence: High.

The counterexample is exact, bounded, rank one, and satisfies the stated assumptions with a fixed coefficient. Its prediction is zero for algebraic reasons, and a strictly positive-noise extension avoids reliance on degeneracy. Independent original-PDF QA confirms the location, assumptions and rejection-level central consequence.

findings.markdown:
**Exact location.** PDF9, Section4.1, Theorem7 (restated PDF47); PDF48, AppendixE.1, Eq126 and its following existence assertion; PDF24–25, Lemma12 and proof; dependent leading-gradient cancellation PDF50, AppendixE.4, Eqs137–138, and Theorem7 proof PDF49–50.

**Claim.** For almost every linearly separable multiclass dataset, every initialization and sufficiently small positive constant stepsize, cross-entropy gradient descent satisfies

    w_k(t) = w_hat_k log(t) + rho_k(t),

where rho_k is bounded and w_hat is the multiclass minimum-Euclidean-norm margin solution. No residual-equation solvability assumption appears in the original theorem.

**Error and evidence.** The proof introduces lifted features v_nk=(A_y_n−A_k)x_n. Eq126 requires a finite vector w_tilde for which

    eta exp(−v_nk^T w_tilde) = alpha_nk

on all active margin constraints, with alpha satisfying the multiclass SVM KKT conditions. The next sentence attributes generic existence to Lemma12. That lemma proves generic support independence and nonzero dual coefficients for unrestricted binary feature matrices. It does not establish generic existence on this structured lifted family.

For fixed labels, the lift is a linear image of the Nd continuous original feature coordinates. Every lifted column has zero sum across its K class blocks. Removing the obvious common-class gauge still leaves N(K−1) columns in intrinsic dimension d(K−1), whose unrestricted ambient parameter space has dimension Nd(K−1)^2. The actual lifted collection has dimension Nd. For K>=3 it therefore occupies a Lebesgue-null subspace even in this gauge-reduced ambient space.

An almost-everywhere statement for arbitrary ambient binary features supplies no almost-everywhere statement for the original x_n on this structured subspace: an ambient exceptional null set can contain the entire subspace and have full-measure preimage. Lemma12's polynomial proof would need a further argument that the relevant degeneracy polynomials are nonzero after imposing the multiclass structure; its unrestricted identity-matrix example does not supply that. The complete original AppendixE contains no such argument or alternative existence proof.

This missing step is used in the proof. PDF50 replaces w_hat by eta times the exponential combination of support features, using Eq126. This cancels the leading 1/t term in the residual update. Lemma20's summable residual bound and the Theorem7 telescoping argument depend on that cancellation. Even replacing termwise Eq126 by the weaker aggregate cancellation equation requires a new existence/genericity argument for the structured family; the original binary lemma does not establish it.

The exact lift-rank checks in `genton-independent-qa.json` verify, for example, K=3,d=2,N=3: original/lift image dimension6, gauge-reduced ambient dimension24, remaining codimension18. An exactly separable fixture x_1=(2,0),x_2=(−1,2),x_3=(−1,−2), labels1/2/3, with class weights equal to these vectors has all six pairwise margins6,6,7,8,7,8. Thus the domain mismatch also occurs in a nonempty open separability regime.

The authors' [2024 primary revision](https://arxiv.org/html/1710.10345v7), Section4.1, independently corroborates this dependency: it acknowledges the invalid binary-to-multiclass transfer, adds residual-equation existence as a theorem assumption, and leaves generic solvability conjectural. The direct original-proof/domain analysis above is the evidence; the later revision is corroboration.

**Reason for rejection.** Unconditional multiclass cross-entropy implicit bias is a distinct main extension advertised in the abstract, Section4.1 and contribution summary on PDF13. The paper presents this guarantee for almost all separable multiclass datasets as proved, but the proof depends on an unestablished existence statement on precisely that target data family. Accepting the paper as written would accept an unsupported central theoretical contribution. Retaining the advertised scope requires new substantive structured-genericity or existence analysis. Adding the presently unproved solvability condition instead withdraws the original guarantee for the claimed dataset class; this is a substantive scope reduction, beyond a typographical or constant correction. The binary results and a conditional multiclass statement can survive without resolving this issue.

**Discovery method.** Traced the finite residual construction and its binary genericity citation while checking the multiclass proof, then located the primary author revision identifying the same transfer problem.

**Verification method.** Read the complete original paper and appendices; inspected rendered original theorem, binary genericity proof, residual equation and cancellation pages. Re-derived the structured-lift dimensions including the common-class gauge quotient. Executed exact rank and separability certificates and independently reviewed the proof dependency. A second auditor checked the original pages, primary revision, dimension calculation and severity rationale.

**Confidence.** High for the unsupported proof dependency and loss of the stated unconditional guarantee: the exact genericity domain and cancellation are directly checkable, independent QA agrees, and the primary revision explicitly changes this scope. This report does **not** demonstrate that Theorem7 is false, exhibit a positive-measure counterexample to residual solvability, refute the binary max-margin result, or invalidate a particular experiment.

 Executables: an unpublished audit file and an unpublished audit file (both exited0). Full-paper notes separately record lower-severity formulation errors, controls, source provenance and empirical replay limits.

sections.title: What may be wrong
sections.html: The proof imports an existence argument for unrestricted binary features into a highly structured multiclass feature family. It does not show that the needed residual equations are solvable there.

sections.title: Evidence in brief
sections.html:
With three classes, two input dimensions, and three observations, the multiclass lift has dimension six inside a gauge-reduced ambient space of dimension 24. A negligible exceptional set in the ambient space may contain the entire structured family. The leading-gradient cancellation therefore relies on an unproved existence step. The record notes that a later author version adds the existence premise rather than proving genericity.

\[ w_k(t)=\widehat w_k\log t+\rho_k(t),\qquad \sup_t\lVert\rho_k(t)\rVert<\infty\quad\text{requires the missing residual-solvability step} \]
